text:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Spectral Consortium (dedicated VPC eu2, tenant=spec-consortium) exceeding p99 latency SLO (target: 450ms, current: ~2.4s). Pager: mia. Reference: runbook#dedicated-latency.
ops-bot: auto-created warroom 2765432100, adding oncall + oncall-escalation policy. Notifying #eng-runtime and #customer-success.
mia (oncall): I'm on it. Confirming: impact is only Spectral's dedicated pool in eu2?
carlos (customer-eng): Yes — customer reports degraded product search and slow chat for enterprise users. They've flagged a live incident to their ops team.
sanjay: I can join for triage, pulling metrics now (q=tenant=spec-consortium, region=eu2). Seeing big spike in request queue length and 10x KV lookups at 11:07 UTC.
jordan (eng-runtime): Drop logs:
```
MODEL: redwood-7b-ft-instruct
POOL: dedicated-eu2-spec-consortium
metric: request_latency_p99=2400ms
metric: inference_queue_len=78
trace: trace_id=0x7f9a3c
error_rate=0.2% (timeouts)
```

jordan (eng-runtime): Also seeing high memcpy wait on the GPUs on the hot hosts — looks like a single tenant burst, not model-wide.
mia (oncall): Customer has 4 dedicated instances (gpus) in their pool. Do we have warm spares in eu2?
leo (infra): Warm spare pool exists but currently scaled to 0 for cost. We can spin up 2 warm spares in eu2 (eta ~4m to healthy). Kicking now.
ops-bot: action: scale-up warm-spares eu2 -> +2 initiated by leo.
alice (solutions): Quick customer note: Spectral's queries are mostly long-context rerank calls right now (context ~6k tokens). Might be pushing KV cache churn. Could be prefix cache misses.
sanjay: I'm seeing a set of ~8000 requests/min with heavy long-context calls originating from a handful of IPs owned by spec-consortium. Correlating with tenant quota spike.
jordan (eng-runtime): Mitigation options:
  1) Temporarily route some traffic from their dedicated pool to a compatible hosted variant (redwood-7b-quant) as fallback (lower perf but lower memory).
  2) Isolate the noisy tenant onto separate set of nodes (tenant isolation) — requires draining and reprovisioning, ~6-10m.
  3) Apply emergency per-tenant rate limit (soft throttle) at the routing layer — instant but visible to customer.
mia (oncall): What's the customer impact for each option?
carlos (customer-eng): 1) Hosted fallback: visible increase in latency for some calls and possible cost shift; customer prefers no errors but will tolerate slightly worse latencies. 2) Isolation: best UX once complete, but ~10m window of instability. 3) Throttle: immediate relief but will drop user requests. Customer ops asks for minimal errors. They prefer graceful slowdown over hard failures.
ops-bot: warm-spares eu2: instance-7 and instance-8 booting (health checks in progress).
leo (infra): warm-spares healthy in 3m 20s, added to routing pool as capacity targets.
sanjay: After warm-spares join, queue length down to 12, p99 dropped to ~900ms. Improvement but still above SLO.
jordan (eng-runtime): Suggest a two-step: 1) add capacity (done), 2) apply short soft-throttles on heaviest endpoints (rerank/long-context) to cut peak tails while we prepare tenant isolation. I'll prepare the throttle rule: route::spec-consortium::endpoint=rerank => rate=120 rps (soft).
mia (oncall): Apply throttle, preferring 429-with-retry-after header and a customer-friendly message. Carlos, can you tell customer ops we are putting a short soft throttle for 10-15m to stabilize?
carlos (customer-eng): Telling them now — will ask them to confirm but they sound OK with a brief soft throttle vs continued high tail.
ops-bot: Applying route throttle: route::spec-consortium::rerank -> 120 rps (soft).
sanjay: Throttle applied. Immediate effect: queue len -> 6, p99 -> 520ms, p95 -> 160ms. Latency still above 450ms p99 but close.
jordan (eng-runtime): While throttle holds, I'm spinning an isolation job: create a new tenant-specific pool, drain 2 noisy hosts, reprovision them with pinned kernel/quantization settings. ETA ~8m.
leo (infra): Provisioning new pool nodes (request id: prov-9a1b). Networking/VPC attachments in progress.
mia (oncall): Noted. If isolation completes, we should lift throttle and monitor for regression. Keep enforcement window <= 15m.
car los (customer-eng): Customer confirms throttle ok for 15m. They requested notification just before we lift it.
ops-bot: prov-9a1b: nodes ready. Starting tenant migration: migrating ~20% of active sessions to new nodes for canary.
jordan (eng-runtime): Canary traffic looks good: p99 on canary nodes ~430ms. Rolling remainder of sessions.
sanjay: After full migration, p99 stabilized to 420ms, p95 150ms. Queue length steady at <=4. Error rate back to baseline.
mia (oncall): Great. Lifting throttle in 30s.
ops-bot: throttle removed for route::spec-consortium::rerank.
carlos (customer-eng): Customer notified — they see performance returning to normal now. Thanks.
jordan (eng-runtime): Root cause notes (prelim): sudden long-context replay from a customer batch job causing KV cache thrash + a GPU memcpy contention pattern on old kernel version. Isolated nodes reprovisioned with updated kernel and kv-cache tuning.
mia (oncall): Next steps:
 - Post-incident: collect perf traces and the offending request patterns (sanjay).
 - Patch: deploy kernel memcpy fix + kv-cache heuristics to eu2 (jordan/leo).
 - Customer follow-up: Carlos to coordinate SLO credits and postmortem call.
 - Runbook update: mark dedicated-pool warm-spares policy to keep 1 spare always warm for enterprise pools > X capacity (mia/alice).

alice (solutions): I'll draft a short customer-facing summary and a timeline for the postmortem.
mia (oncall): Thanks everyone. I'll close the warroom once we have the postmortem link.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT 2765432100 updated -> status: mitigated, severity: P2, assigned: mia.
